# QQQ

> A capability-secure WebAssembly Component Model runtime. This file is a **curated index**: it says what exists and what order to read it in. It is generated by `tools/gen_llms_txt.py` from the file listing, so it cannot describe a file that is not there.

For the documentation concatenated into one document, see [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt).

Sizes are **LF-normalised content byte counts**, identical on every platform regardless of the checkout's line endings. Documents above 100 KB are labelled `large` instead of being measured: they change on every commit, and a number would go stale.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md) — What QQQ is, in one page. _(human)_ (11 KB)
- [QQQ-Proposal-V1.md](QQQ-Proposal-V1.md) — The full specification. Every other document derives from this one; section numbers are stable and are cited by the checklist. (large)

## What is built, and what was learned building it

- [QQQ-Checklist-V1.md](QQQ-Checklist-V1.md) — The 586 tracked items, each citing the Proposal section that governs it, with the evidence for each completed one. (large)
- [QQQ-Observations-and-Memories.md](QQQ-Observations-and-Memories.md) — Decisions, observations, mistakes and corrections made while building. Read this to learn what was tried and rejected, and why. (large)

## The machine contracts (for an agent)

- [docs/errors.md](docs/errors.md) — Every `QQQ-XXXX` error code with its cause and remediation. _(agent)_ (14 KB)
- [docs/wit-reference.md](docs/wit-reference.md) — Every WIT package, interface, function and type, generated from `wit/`. _(agent)_ (17 KB)
- [schema/qqq-toml.schema.json](schema/qqq-toml.schema.json) — JSON Schema for `qqq.toml`, generated from the Rust type that parses it. _(agent)_ (21 KB)
- [schema/qqq-lock.schema.json](schema/qqq-lock.schema.json) — JSON Schema for `qqq.lock`, including the per-package `caps` record. _(agent)_ (9 KB)
- [schema/cli-envelope.schema.json](schema/cli-envelope.schema.json) — JSON Schema for the `--json` envelope every command emits. _(agent)_ (1 KB)

## Using it

- [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) — Index of the documentation directory, with what each file is for. _(human)_ (6 KB)
- [docs/glossary.md](docs/glossary.md) — The 18 defined terms. Several are load-bearing and mean something narrower here than in general use. (3 KB)
- [docs/threat-model.md](docs/threat-model.md) — The adversaries QQQ defends against, and what it explicitly does not. (11 KB)
- [docs/out-of-scope.md](docs/out-of-scope.md) — What is deliberately not defended, so absences are decisions rather than oversights. (7 KB)
- [docs/contributing/claims-policy.md](docs/contributing/claims-policy.md) — How a factual claim must be verified before it enters a document. _(human)_ (7 KB)
- [docs/contributing/anchors.md](docs/contributing/anchors.md) — The anchor convention, and why a retired section is tombstoned rather than deleted. _(human)_ (6 KB)

## The machinery behind the documents

- [docs/abi-cost-measured.md](docs/abi-cost-measured.md) — The measured ABI-crossing costs (`PERF-005`), replacing the estimates in §9.3, with the environment, the estimate-by-estimate comparison, and an explicit statement of what was not measured. (19 KB)
- [docs/verified-facts.md](docs/verified-facts.md) — Facts asserted in the Proposal, each classified by how perishable it is and when it was last checked. (8 KB)
- [docs/reconciliation.md](docs/reconciliation.md) — Corrections made to the Proposal, with the reasoning. (4 KB)
- [docs/wasmtime-advisory-process.md](docs/wasmtime-advisory-process.md) — How a Wasmtime security advisory is handled. _(human)_ (11 KB)
- [docs/wasmtime-upgrade-runbook.md](docs/wasmtime-upgrade-runbook.md) — How a scheduled Wasmtime upgrade is taken: the steps, their evidence, and the behaviours an upgrade can change without breaking the build. _(human)_ (8 KB)
- [docs/unsafe-audit.md](docs/unsafe-audit.md) — The `unsafe` audit: what it covers and what it has found. _(human)_ (6 KB)
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — How to report a vulnerability, and what response to expect. _(human)_ (5 KB)
- [docs/development-bridge.md](docs/development-bridge.md) — How the Linux verification bridge works, and the one-way rule it enforces on build output. _(human)_ (11 KB)
- [docs/adr/README.md](docs/adr/README.md) — Architecture decision records: what was decided, and what was rejected. _(human)_ (4 KB)
- [docs/advisories/README.md](docs/advisories/README.md) — How a dependency advisory is recorded and resolved. _(human)_ (4 KB)
- [docs/advisories/INDEX.md](docs/advisories/INDEX.md) — The advisory register itself. _(agent)_ (1 KB)
- [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) — The non-negotiables the design is held to. _(human)_ (6 KB)

## Repository layout

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `crates/` | The Rust workspace, one directory per crate. |
| `wit/` | WIT interface definitions, one file per package. |
| `schema/` | Generated JSON Schemas (see `CON-016`). |
| `docs/` | Documentation. `docs/README.md` indexes it. |
| `tools/` | Checkers and generators, each with a `--self-test`. |
| `docker/` | The Linux verification bridge. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | The gate. Nine jobs. |
